duplicate_work: Same request could validate the same auth session in multiple middleware layers and again in route dependencies.
Each validation could re-read auth session and user rows.
C18F permission isolation then performed active membership validation again.
permission registry lookup repeated per dependency invocation.
enabled user assignment resolution repeated per dependency invocation.
role default lookup repeated even when only count metadata was needed.
data isolation reused C18F org_id when available but still revalidated the same session.
org_context listed visible module bindings for the org.
C18F permission isolation then fetched the requested module binding again.

duplicate_db_query_points: auth session validation in org_context, permission, data_isolation, and get_current_session
User lookup in validate_session and UnifiedPermissionEngine
Active org membership lookup in org_context and C18F
Module binding lookup in org_context module_scope and C18F
User assignment lookup in each permission-key decision
Role default lookup in each permission-key decision

post_change_chain.org_module_resolution: user and active membership resolve through request org_context when present, otherwise one joined query
post_change_chain.module_resolution: request org_context.module_scope is reused before querying module_bindings
post_change_chain.permission_key_resolution: user, registry, role defaults, and enabled assignments reuse request cache and 45 second TTL cache

remaining_non_duplicate_checks: Control-plane C16 admin guard remains a separate boundary from route-specific RBAC checks.
Semantically different route permissions are evaluated under distinct cache keys.
Internal system RBAC uses check_internal_permission without request state because it is not part of the HTTP middleware chain.
